mbm-1126.clue: I can hear a high score from the hall.
mbm-1126.quote: My old puzzle game plays three rising notes when I clear a stage. Dad whistles a fourth from the kitchen. I leave the door open during the hard stages because his note is the best one.

mbm-1127.clue: I borrow the beat from a rocking chair.
mbm-1127.quote: My grandmother’s chair creaks twice with each backward rock. I played son on my little guitar beside it and found the perfect place for the bass to come in. She kept rocking until we got it right.

mbm-1128.clue: I take notes in the blank spaces.
mbm-1128.quote: I bought a used field guide with empty margins. The previous owner had marked one page with a pressed leaf. I drew the tree outside my window beside it, so the leaf would have company.

mbm-1129.clue: I lost a point to the afternoon sun.
mbm-1129.quote: I looked up for a beach volleyball serve and saw my brother’s kite floating right over the ball. I missed completely. In his photograph the kite has a perfectly round blue nose.

mbm-1130.clue: I brought my chair to the corner shop.
mbm-1130.quote: The sunny patch in my courtyard disappears before lunch. My neighbor offered the little bench outside his shop. I sit there with my sun hat and let him know when the peaches need turning.

mbm-1131.clue: I build the city before anybody arrives.
mbm-1131.quote: My favorite board game is a town made from little cardboard streets. I set it out early and walk my finger from the station to the square. That way I know where to invite everybody for tea.

mbm-1132.clue: One of my mecha wears old paint.
mbm-1132.quote: I brushed fresh silver onto a model’s armor and rubbed the edges until the first blue coat showed through. My brother said it looked like it remembered its last adventure. That was the nicest review I got.

mbm-1133.clue: I joined the dance a beat late.
mbm-1133.quote: At my first folk-dance night I missed the step every time the circle came round. The oldest dancer squeezed my hand just before the turn. By the last song I was passing the squeeze to somebody else.

mbm-1134.clue: I put a streetlight beside the giant.
mbm-1134.quote: I made a wire lamp no taller than my thumb for a mecha display. It lights up the robot’s boots and the tiny umbrella of the person waiting below. The giant looks positively neighborly at night.

mbm-1135.clue: I like the plane before it wakes.
mbm-1135.quote: I arrive at the little airstrip before the tow tractor comes out. Once a dragonfly rested on a training plane’s wingtip, another flyer doing its morning check. I drew them both in the same box.

mbm-1136.clue: I learned to watch the bare branch.
mbm-1136.quote: For weeks I mistook a flash of orange for a bird. One day I kept my binoculars on the branch after the leaves fell and a real robin landed. This time I got to sketch its feet.

mbm-1137.clue: I know where the steam goes.
mbm-1137.quote: At the mountain onsen I watched a ribbon of steam slip between two pine branches. A drop gathered on one needle and fell back into the bath. I let my next train go by.

mbm-1138.quote: I filled my third juggling bag with less rice by mistake. It lingers in the air, just enough for a little bow before I catch it. The mistake has become the official ending of my routine.

mbm-1139.clue: I stitched one row by candlelight.
mbm-1139.quote: We lost the lights during quilting night and finished the border by the glow from a jam jar. In daylight one blue strip turned out purple. None of us would let the others unpick it.

mbm-1140.clue: I set a paper cup on the floor.
mbm-1140.quote: My spotter used a little cup of water to mark where my feet start for a lift. After weeks of practice the cup stays full. I pour it on the plant by the gym door before I go.

mbm-1141.clue: My pencil got a better score than I did.
mbm-1141.quote: At mini golf I tried to sketch the angle to the cup. My pencil rolled off the clipboard, followed the ramp and dropped in. The attendant offered me a tiny scorecard for the pencil.

mbm-1142.clue: I run when the roofs are pink.
mbm-1142.quote: At sunrise my route goes past four tin roofs. I try to catch each while it’s still pink. I’ve yet to catch all four, which gives me an excellent reason to set the alarm.

mbm-1143.clue: I sing the high part to an empty chair.
mbm-1143.quote: At home I place Dad’s old wooden chair opposite mine and practice his harmony. When he comes round I give him the chair and let him catch all the little changes I’ve made.

mbm-1144.clue: I know the train by the dust on its windows.
mbm-1144.quote: The quarry line has one green carriage that comes back gray. Once rain left a great clean streak down the middle. I sketched the green stripe before the engine carried it into the tunnel.

mbm-1145.clue: I keep the first ball in the flowerpot.
mbm-1145.quote: I made a hole-in-one at the miniature lighthouse the day my mother came to watch. She planted a daisy beside the ball in her little sand-colored pot. My trophy has bloomed twice.

mbm-1146.clue: I made a cup to fit a glove.
mbm-1146.quote: My brother asked for a mug he could hold outdoors in winter. I shaped its wide handle around his woolly mitten. The thumbprint on the clay is knit in tiny blue stitches.

mbm-1147.clue: I always play the uphill hole twice.
mbm-1147.quote: I putted the ball so gently it crawled up to the top, paused, and rolled straight back to my shoe. My niece cackled. I paid for another round just to see whether I could do it again.

mbm-1148.clue: I still have one spoonful left.
mbm-1148.quote: The ice-cream contest ended just as a scoop dropped into my shirt pocket. Grandma insisted it counted as a takeaway. I washed the pocket out and sewed a tiny cherry above the stain.

mbm-1149.clue: I keep count with red jellybeans.
mbm-1149.quote: My brother sets a red sweet on the scoring table after every spare I make at bowling. We share them on the bus home. On my best night we needed a paper bag.

mbm-1150.clue: I dance the last bar backward.
mbm-1150.quote: My partner taught me to lead by swapping places during practice. Walking backward into a waltz made me feel every tiny pause. When we swapped back she said I had finally learned to listen.
